entries.why_it_matters: Ukraine has been begging for more interceptors to protect its cities from Russian ballistic missiles. Those missiles are now getting through, and Ukrainians are being killed because the air defenses needed to stop them are running out.

entries.what_happened: U.S. private employers added just 44,000 jobs in July, well below the 75,000 economists expected and down from 95,000 in June. Leisure and hospitality lost 11,000 jobs.

Judge Amit Mehta “reluctantly” dismissed the final eight Jan. 6 cases against Oath Keepers leader Stewart Rhodes and other members after Trump’s Justice Department moved to drop the charges. Mehta said the decision gives them “unearned grace” and closes the last prosecutions seeking accountability for the attack on the Capitol.

entries.why_it_matters: An international human rights body that investigates abuses across the Americas is now examining the U.S. over its treatment of protesters and journalists. What began as an immigration crackdown is being used against people who protest, document, or criticize it.

entries.what_happened: Trump’s DOJ agreed with Louisiana officials to end 61 years of federal desegregation oversight of Bossier Parish Schools. DOJ spent decades enforcing these orders but now calls them federal intrusion into local schools.
entries.why_it_matters: Federal oversight existed because local officials could not be trusted to dismantle segregation on their own. Now the DOJ is walking away from one of the federal government’s most important tools for enforcing equal protection in public schools.

entries.what_happened: ICE detained 21-year-old Laura Rojas Ortiz and her infant son during a routine check-in and has held them for more than 40 days. Rojas Ortiz is five months pregnant with what her family says is a high-risk pregnancy, and has reportedly received no ultrasound, blood tests, or specialist care.

A federal lawsuit alleges Trump officials are accelerating deportations of unaccompanied migrant children, including survivors of trafficking and abuse who qualify for legal protections in the U.S. Some children have reportedly been ordered deported even after being approved for protected immigration status.
entries.why_it_matters: These protections exist specifically to keep abused and trafficked children from being sent back into danger. Trump officials are pushing to deport them anyway in their cruel drive to increase deportation numbers.

entries.what_happened: DHS is hiring private investigators to track down deported immigrants in their home countries, photograph their homes, and collect information from them. DHS says it is targeting people who still owe immigration related fines after leaving the U.S.

Nearly half the staff at the DOJ office responsible for investigating attorney misconduct has left during Trump’s second term, while new investigations have fallen to a 20-year low. At the same time, misconduct complaints have hit a 20-year high, with federal judges accusing DOJ lawyers of false statements, defying court orders, and using the legal system against political opponents.
entries.why_it_matters: Misconduct allegations inside DOJ are soaring at the same time the office responsible for investigating them is being gutted. That leaves DOJ lawyers with fewer consequences for abusing their power.

entries.what_happened: Trump officials are moving to eliminate most of Head Start’s 133 pages of federal requirements, including standards for class sizes, math and literacy instruction, medical and dental screenings, and home visits. Head Start currently provides early education, health care, and other support to roughly 700,000 low-income children.
entries.why_it_matters: Head Start was created to provide poor children with more than basic child care, including education, health screenings, nutrition, and family support. Trump officials are stripping away many of the standards that make those services part of the program.

entries.what_happened: The Pentagon removed 25 years of unclassified weapons testing reports from public access, including reports exposing performance, maintenance, and safety problems. The Pentagon has also cut its independent testing office from 126 employees to 30 and removed 90 weapons programs from its oversight.

Trump reportedly confronted Pete Hegseth after learning that severe munitions shortages are limiting U.S. military options against Iran. The U.S. has nearly exhausted some critical weapons, including ATACMS missiles, while shortages of Patriot and other air-defense interceptors are leaving barely any available for Ukraine.
entries.source_name: The Washington Post and The Atlantic

entries.what_happened: Suspected Iran-backed hackers have targeted water systems in at least 12 states, including more than 30 systems in Minnesota. Hackers gained remote access to pumps, valves, and water pressure controls, forcing some utilities to operate manually. Federal investigators are continuing to investigate and have not officially blamed Iran.

The State Department plans to close U.S. missions in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia, and Cameroon as Trump continues shrinking America’s diplomatic presence abroad. More than half of U.S. ambassadorial posts worldwide are vacant.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is pulling America back from places where China is competing for influence. China already has a diplomatic presence in three of the five countries the U.S. is abandoning, handing Beijing more room to fill the vacuum.

entries.what_happened: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said trade negotiations with the U.S. have turned “nasty” as Trump threatens additional tariffs and publicly attacks Canada’s leadership. Carney said the countries are now “in the middle of a tariff war.”

New U.S. intelligence warns that Putin could test NATO with a cyberattack, hybrid operation, or limited military incursion sometime between this fall and 2029. The warning comes as U.S. stocks of Patriot, THAAD, SM-3, Stinger, and other critical weapons are severely depleted.

Millions of children could lose access to free school meals after Trump’s tax cuts for the wealthy law cut SNAP enrollment and severed the automatic link between food stamps and free school meals. An estimated 1.5 million children have already lost SNAP benefits, while as many as 18.3 million students could lose access to free school meals.

ICE and TSA have dramatically expanded immigration enforcement at U.S. airports as Trump pushes for 2,000 arrests a day, including detaining people with pending asylum, visa, and green card applications. Some airline workers are refusing to cooperate without proper legal authority. Southwest employees, for example, blocked an ICE agent from boarding a plane without a judicial warrant.

entries.what_happened: ICE said that all field officers will have body cameras by the end of August, but the agency can withhold footage of shootings and other serious incidents unless releasing it is in ICE’s “best interests.” The ICE director can block or indefinitely delay footage, and released videos will conceal officers’ faces, names, and badge numbers.
entries.why_it_matters: ICE has repeatedly acted as if the rules don’t apply to it, and this policy makes accountability even harder. The agency can now decide whether the public gets to see evidence of its own officers’ misconduct based on whether releasing it is in ICE’s “best interests.”

entries.what_happened: Republican megadonor Palmer Luckey, co-founder of defense contractor Anduril, has donated $5.9 million to the party while his company receives billions in federal contracts. In March, the Army awarded Anduril a $20 billion sole-source drone contract, and the company could also compete for Trump’s Golden Dome missile defense project.
entries.why_it_matters: Luckey is raising millions for Republicans while his company is getting billions from the government. It is classic pay-to-play cronyism where major political donors gain access and influence while taxpayer money flows to their businesses.

entries.what_happened: Trump officials awarded a $150 million no-bid contract to the 24-attorney Burke Law Group to represent unaccompanied immigrant children after ending contracts with dozens of organizations that previously provided those services. Only two of the firm’s attorneys specialize in immigration and asylum law, while two of its leaders have served in Trump’s government.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump officials took legal services for vulnerable immigrant children away from experienced organizations and handed $150 million, without competitive bidding, to a politically connected firm with little immigration expertise. Trump allies get a massive government contract while children facing deportation pay the price.

entries.what_happened: The SEC moved to dismiss its insider trading lawsuit against former healthcare executive Terren Peizer, who was convicted of insider trading and securities fraud and sentenced to 3.5 years in prison. Trump pardoned Peizer in January.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s pardon already erased Peizer’s criminal punishment, and now the government is dropping the civil case against him too, removing another consequence for crimes a federal jury found he committed.

entries.what_happened: The Senate narrowly confirmed Todd Blanche as attorney general after he repeatedly argued that Trump has broad constitutional authority to direct the Justice Department, including ordering investigations. When asked about DOJ independence during his confirmation hearing, Blanche pointed to Article II and said executive power belongs to Trump.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump has put his former personal lawyer in charge of a Justice Department he has already used to target his enemies and protect his allies. Blanche believes Trump can direct investigations and prosecutions. DOJ independence is effectively gone, leaving federal law enforcement in the hands of a Trump loyalist.

entries.what_happened: Trump revived his effort to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over “mortgage fraud” allegations she denies, two months after the Supreme Court blocked his previous attempt because she had not been given enough opportunity to respond. The White House has now given Cook 21 days to answer the allegations before Trump decides whether to remove her.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump wants the Fed to lower interest rates and is again trying to remove a governor who stands in his way. Replacing Cook would give him another chance to install a loyalist and bring an institution that is supposed to operate independently of the president further under his control.

entries.what_happened: The Pentagon revoked former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall’s eligibility to access classified information, accusing him of revealing sensitive information about Trump’s Qatari Air Force One. Kendall denies disclosing classified information and says he has not been told what he allegedly revealed.
entries.why_it_matters: Kendall publicly raised security concerns about Trump’s Qatari plane, and now the Pentagon is stripping his security clearance over information it has not even identified. The government is once again using its power to punish someone who criticized Trump.

entries.what_happened: Trump publicly called on U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro to revive charges against a former Olympian accused of vandalizing the Reflecting Pool. Prosecutors dropped the case after finding evidence that faulty installation, not vandalism, may have caused the damage, but Trump insists a crime occurred and has criticized Pirro for dropping it.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is publicly ordering a federal prosecutor to reconsider a criminal case after her office found the evidence did not support it. Criminal prosecutions are supposed to follow the evidence, not the president’s personal demands.

entries.what_happened: The State Department is reportedly expanding social media screening to foreign journalists applying for U.S. visas and requiring them to make their accounts public for government review. The move follows new limits on how long foreign journalists can remain in the country.
entries.why_it_matters: Foreign journalists now have to consider whether their reporting on Trump or his government could jeopardize their ability to enter and work in the U.S. That gives the government enormous power to punish or deter journalists whose coverage it doesn’t like.

entries.what_happened: Pete Hegseth has blocked at least 40 high-ranking military promotions from reaching the Senate, roughly half involving women and people of color. Women now account for just 4% of nominations for general and admiral positions this year, the lowest share in at least 25 years.
entries.why_it_matters: Hegseth is personally intervening in promotions while openly attacking diversity in the military. Women are reaching lower officer ranks in record numbers, but their path to the military’s highest ranks is being narrowed.

entries.what_happened: ICE ended a policy requiring it to report and investigate deaths that occur within 30 days of release from detention. Prisciliano Trejo Ricano, 29, became critically ill in ICE custody and died from acute leukemia eight days after his release, but his death does not appear in ICE’s official count.
entries.why_it_matters: ICE can now release gravely ill detainees and leave them out of its death count if they die days later. The government has created a way to hide deaths connected to its brutal detention system.

entries.what_happened: Trump has deported more than 1,200 people to Vietnam and 400 to Laos, more than during the previous three presidential terms combined. Many came to the U.S. legally as children after the Vietnam War and are now being deported decades later over old criminal convictions after Trump pressured both countries to accept them.

New Jersey opened a civil rights investigation into GEO Group’s treatment of detainees at Delaney Hall, days after Edwin Lopez-Cornejo died following a medical emergency. His family says he was not receiving necessary medication. The privately run ICE facility has faced other allegations of inadequate medical care, spoiled food, and unsanitary conditions.

Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza, commander of the Army’s V Corps overseeing U.S. forces and operations across Europe, was abruptly removed nearly two months before his scheduled departure. The Army has not explained why, and Costanza joins more than two dozen senior military officers removed or sidelined under Pete Hegseth.
entries.why_it_matters: V Corps helps coordinate U.S. forces along NATO’s eastern flank and provide support for Ukraine as Russia escalates its attacks across Europe. Removing its commander without explanation adds another senior officer to Hegseth’s growing purge of military leadership at a very dangerous moment.

entries.what_happened: Trump is considering an executive order on vaccines and autism as his regime continues investigating a connection despite decades of research involving millions of people finding no credible link. Trump has reportedly pressed RFK Jr. privately about whether he believes he can prove such a conspiracy.

Oil prices rose Sunday after Iran issued sweeping demands for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including an end to U.S. attacks, withdrawal of U.S. forces from the region, sanctions relief, and compensation for war damages. Tankers have been unable to use the strait, which normally carries about 20% of global oil supplies, since fighting resumed in July.

Greenland issued a “strong warning” after Greenland Energy, a Texas oil company linked to Trump, brought drilling equipment ashore without government approval. The company claims the area could hold $1 trillion in oil and is preparing to drill as Trump renews threats to seize control of Greenland.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is threatening to invade Greenland while a company tied to his circle is preparing to exploit its oil without permission. His threats against Greenland are unfolding alongside private efforts to profit from its natural resources.

entries.what_happened: Trump officials have directed U.S. intelligence agencies to identify a current or former Cuban official who could take power in Havana and cooperate with the U.S. At the same time, Trump is pressuring Cuba to open its economy to U.S. businesses, buy American oil, and expel Russian and Chinese intelligence operatives.

U.S. intelligence assesses that an explosive-laden drone found near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Germany’s Leipzig/Halle Airport likely belonged to the Russian government. The discovery forced the airport to shut down, and German reports say the drone failed to detonate.

The U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, far below economists’ forecast of 95,000 new jobs, while May and June were revised down by another 103,000. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, largely because people left the workforce.

Democratic turnout for House primaries in Shelby County, which includes Memphis, more than doubled from 2024 and reached its highest level in a decade. The surge followed Tennessee Republicans’ decision to dismantle the state’s only majority Black congressional district and divide its voters among three districts after the Supreme Court eroded Voting Rights Act protections.

entries.what_happened: The White House released previously classified FBI documents as part of Trump’s campaign against officials who investigated Russia’s 2016 election attack. Instead, the records revealed that the FBI opened a separate counterintelligence investigation in 2017 to determine whether Trump was “directed by, controlled by, and/or coordinated activities with” Russia. The inquiry was sidetracked before it could be investigated.

Guren “Bobby” Zhou, a businessman under investigation in Britain for alleged money laundering, invested $100 million in Trump’s World Liberty Financial through a newly created company. As much as $75 million went to a company controlled by Trump and his sons.
entries.why_it_matters: A businessman under investigation for alleged money laundering put $100 million into Trump’s crypto business, with as much as $75 million flowing to Trump and his sons. And the source of the money is unknown.

entries.what_happened: A development group backed by Jared Kushner paid more than $120 million for Albanian beachfront property despite villagers warning Kushner that the seller, Artur Shehu, had stolen the land and that its ownership had been disputed for years. Two months later, Albanian prosecutors sought Shehu’s arrest, accusing him of helping lead an international cocaine trafficking operation and laundering money through stolen property, including the land sold to Kushner.
entries.why_it_matters: Kushner was directly warned that the land was allegedly stolen and went ahead with the $120 million deal anyway. Now the man his group paid is wanted in an international drug trafficking and money laundering investigation involving the same property.

entries.what_happened: A federal judge dismissed fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani at the DOJ’s request but criticized the “irregularities” behind the decision. A political appointee overrode career prosecutors after consulting largely with Adani’s lawyers, who said he would invest $10 billion in the U.S. if the charges were dropped.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s DOJ dropped a major fraud case after the defendant’s lawyers promised billions in investment. When money and political connections can override career prosecutors, the Justice Department becomes a system where the powerful can buy their way out of accountability.

entries.what_happened: Trump has repeatedly called Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh since his confirmation in May, asking about his economic forecasts and views while publicly demanding lower interest rates.
entries.why_it_matters: The Fed is supposed to operate independently of the president. Trump picked Warsh, is demanding lower rates, and is calling him directly about the economy. He is again openly pressuring and trying to take control of an independent institution.

entries.what_happened: Ninety percent of Trump’s ambassador nominees in his second term are political appointees rather than career diplomats, the highest share of any modern presidency. Many are wealthy donors or political allies, while more than 100 U.S. diplomatic posts remain without confirmed ambassadors.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is turning ambassadorships into rewards for donors and loyalists at an unprecedented rate. Experience is being replaced by money and political loyalty in the people representing the U.S. abroad.

entries.what_happened: The State Department has revoked more than 175,000 visas, including over criminal allegations, immigration violations, social media activity, and comments officials deemed threatening or supportive of violence. It has also expanded social media screening and vetting of visa holders and applicants.

ICE plans to pay LexisNexis $6.7 million for access to more than 82 billion public and proprietary records that can be fed into Palantir and other ICE systems. The contract also calls for AI identity tools and facial recognition capable of searching massive image databases.
entries.why_it_matters: ICE is building a surveillance state, combining billions of records, facial recognition, AI, and Palantir to identify people, map their connections, and track their movements and where they live. Once built, that system can be used to track and target far more than immigrants.

entries.what_happened: A cybersecurity firm hired to examine voting systems found serious vulnerabilities but no evidence that votes were altered or the systems exploited. Officials initially approved an expansion of the work, but the project was abruptly terminated after Trump officials and allies pushed researchers to find evidence supporting lies of election manipulation.

Trump officials indefinitely froze dozens of completed Education Department civil rights investigations involving racial harassment, sexual harassment, and violence in schools. Over the past 18 months, the Office for Civil Rights has reached just three settlements involving racial harassment and none involving sexual harassment or violence after Trump gutted the office and redirected its resources.
entries.why_it_matters: Students reported racial abuse, sexual harassment, and violence, and their cases were close to being resolved. Trump gutted the office responsible for investigating them, leaving students without answers or accountability.

entries.what_happened: ICE arrested Iliana Lick, a 30-year-old Argentine woman living and working as a nanny in Philadelphia, as she prepared to fly to a World Cup match. Lick entered the U.S. legally and has a pending immigration application, but DHS claims she overstayed her visa and transferred her to an ICE detention facility in New Mexico.

More than 60 congressional Democrats launched an investigation after an AP review found immigration authorities have detained more than 50 spouses and parents of active duty U.S. service members. Trump rolled back longstanding protections for military families, forcing some troops to take leave or delay deployments after their spouses were detained.

Trump signed an executive order calling for reducing the number of vaccines recommended for all children from 18 diseases to 11, spacing out shots, and breaking up the combined measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine. He again linked vaccines to autism despite extensive research finding no causal connection.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is using presidential power to rewrite childhood vaccine policy around conspiracies that science has repeatedly disproven. Medical experts warn the changes will leave more children vulnerable to preventable diseases.

entries.what_happened: The U.S. Attorney’s Office in Los Angeles hired Shawn Christopher Lewis, a former aide to top federal prosecutor Bill Essayli, as a liaison to local law enforcement despite three DUI convictions and a pending battery charge. Lewis was still on probation for his third DUI when he was arrested for allegedly repeatedly punching a man and preventing him from calling 911.
entries.why_it_matters: A federal prosecutor hired a political ally with three DUI convictions and a pending battery case to work directly with law enforcement. In Trump’s government, loyalty and connections matter more than qualifications, conduct, or basic standards.

entries.what_happened: More than 60 House Democrats are demanding answers from VA Secretary Doug Collins after hundreds of mental health providers left without being replaced. Remaining therapists report being overwhelmed, with some individual appointments cut to as little as 16 minutes and group sessions growing to as many as 35 veterans.

Negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz are at risk of collapsing as Iran and Trump trade escalating demands. Iran wants U.S. attacks and the blockade ended, sanctions lifted, frozen assets released, and compensation for war damages, while Trump is demanding Iran pay for deaths and destruction across the Middle East.

Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia are tightening security around critical infrastructure after warnings that Russia could attack using Ukrainian drones and blame Kyiv. Dams, power plants, natural gas facilities, and other strategic sites are being protected amid growing warnings of Russian sabotage operations.

U.S. bond yields remain near their highest levels in two decades as investors weigh inflation, Trump’s tariffs, his Iran war, rising federal debt, and uncertainty over the Fed. Higher Treasury yields are keeping borrowing costs elevated, including mortgage rates for homebuyers.

entries.what_happened: Trump declined to rule out declaring a national security emergency to impose new rules on the 2026 midterms after an interviewer suggested using emergency powers to require voter ID and proof of citizenship and restrict mail-in voting. Trump responded, “Stranger things have happened,” and said he would “leave it at that.”
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is openly considering using emergency powers to seize control over the midterms. Using presidential power to manipulate the rules of an election is straight out of the authoritarian playbook.

entries.what_happened: Trump Media is selling trading firms faster, automated access to Trump’s Truth Social posts for up to $100,000 a month. More than 10 customers have signed up, potentially giving traders an advantage when Trump posts market-moving announcements on tariffs, foreign policy, or other government actions.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump controls policies that move markets, and his company is charging Wall Street firms for faster access when he announces them. He continues to use the presidency to line his pockets and is so emboldened he doesn’t even bother to hide it.

entries.what_happened: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito made between $390,000 and $2.9 million from fossil fuel interests between 2005 and 2024, according to an analysis of his financial disclosures. He has refused calls to recuse himself from a major case that could shield oil and gas companies from climate lawsuits.

A federal judge issued a nationwide order blocking Trump from using the Postal Service to potentially refuse delivery of mail ballots in states that reject his election directives. The judge said Trump was attempting to “unconstitutionally insert” the executive branch into election regulation months before the midterms.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is trying to seize control of midterms, including over how lawful ballots are handled. Courts are blocking these efforts, but the bigger question is whether Trump will obey those rulings.

entries.what_happened: White House officials asked DOJ to explore prosecuting Olympic canoeist David Hearn again after U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro dropped the case and acknowledged that a botched renovation, not vandalism, caused the damage. Trump publicly attacked Pirro and demanded that she revisit the case.
entries.why_it_matters: Prosecutors concluded there was no evidence, but Trump wants the man prosecuted anyway. The White House continues to weaponize the DOJ to pursue Trump’s enemies while shielding his allies.

entries.what_happened: Trump nominated Project 2025 co-author Dennis Kirk as Interior Department inspector general, where he would oversee investigations into the agency. Democrats are currently seeking an inspector general investigation into Interior’s botched Reflecting Pool renovation and its use of no-bid contracts.

The Treasury Department finalized a rule exempting U.S. companies and individuals from requirements to disclose their true owners, rolling back a major 2021 anti-money laundering law. FinCEN will also delete ownership information Americans previously submitted.
entries.why_it_matters: Shell companies are used to hide dirty money, evade sanctions, commit fraud, and launder criminal proceeds. Trump is eliminating one of the government’s most important tools for finding out who is actually behind them.

entries.what_happened: ICE plans to spend up to $20 million on thousands of gloves that allow officers to deliver painful electric shocks through direct contact with a person’s skin. The devices are designed to force compliance and could reach officers by March.
entries.why_it_matters: ICE is giving its lawless officers another way to inflict pain while operating with virtually no accountability for abuse. Electric shock gloves give agents even more power to use violence against people in their custody.

entries.what_happened: Four human rights groups sued Trump over sanctions imposed on the International Criminal Court, arguing they illegally punish organizations and individuals for working with the court. The groups say the sanctions violate constitutional rights to free speech, association, and religion.

Federal judges have ruled against ICE’s detention tactics more than 16,000 times over the past year after Trump officials expanded mandatory detention to people who previously could seek bond. At least 469 federal judges have concluded the policy is unlawful, while emergency cases have overwhelmed courts nationwide.
entries.why_it_matters: The government continues using a detention policy that hundreds of federal judges have found unlawful. Ignoring thousands of court rulings is another sign that the rule of law is optional for Trump and his officials.

entries.what_happened: Trump’s EEOC is moving to eliminate a 60-year-old requirement that tens of thousands of employers report workforce data by race, gender, and job category. Regulators use the data to identify patterns of workplace discrimination and enforce civil rights laws.

U.S. forces fired two Hellfire missiles into a Panama-flagged cargo ship after it ignored warnings and attempted to enter an Iranian port in violation of Trump’s blockade. The U.S. has now redirected 55 commercial ships, disabled three, and boarded two since the blockade was reimposed in July.

Iran is using waves of drones and maneuvering missiles to overwhelm U.S. air defenses, forcing the Pentagon to rapidly burn through Patriot interceptors. More than 1,500 have been used, with fewer than 1,700 left. Last month, an Iranian missile penetrated U.S. defenses in Jordan, killing three American soldiers and wounding more than 100.
entries.why_it_matters: Iran is getting better at penetrating U.S. defenses while Trump’s war burns through critical interceptors faster than America can replace them. American troops are increasingly vulnerable, while depleted stockpiles leave the U.S. less prepared for the next crisis or conflict.

entries.what_happened: Germany’s top military officer, Gen. Carsten Breuer, said Russia is systematically using drones and other hybrid attacks to probe NATO defenses and identify weaknesses for a future conflict. He said Russia is already shifting its economy and military to prepare for a wider war with the West.

Mortgage delinquencies have reached their highest level since 2015, while serious auto loan delinquencies are at their highest since 2010. Americans are facing high prices, sluggish job growth, and higher gas prices from Trump’s Iran war.
Existing home sales fell 1.7% in July as higher mortgage rates continued to push buyers out of the market. The median home price rose to $434,100, the second-highest level on record.

A judge ordered the Kennedy Center to pay $252,000 in legal fees after it unsuccessfully sued jazz musician Chuck Redd, who withdrew from a performance after the center was renamed after Trump. The judge previously dismissed the lawsuit because the center failed to establish that Redd had a binding contract.

entries.what_happened: An ICE agent pointed a gun at Virginia therapist Carolina Molina after she shouted insults at agents during an immigration operation. entries.why_it_matters: A federal agent pointed a gun at a U.S. citizen after she criticized ICE, and DHS then portrayed her as a dangerous “agitator” who tried to run agents over. Once again, the abuse was caught on video, exposing the lies used to justify it.

entries.what_happened: The Intercept and Freedom of the Press Foundation sued Trump over a Truth Social service selling faster access to his posts for up to $100,000 a month. entries.why_it_matters: Trump controls policies that moves markets while his company profits from selling faster access to his announcements. The lawsuit is challenging one of the more blatant ways Trump is using the presidency to enrich himself and his family.

entries.what_happened: Trump’s Treasury Department finalized a rule exempting U.S. companies and individuals from requirements to disclose their true owners to FinCEN, making permanent the rollback of a major anti-money laundering safeguard. Treasury will also delete beneficial ownership information previously submitted by Americans from the government database.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has expanded DHS’s role in investigating “voter fraud,” deploying Homeland Security Investigations agents to pursue voter records and threatening election officials with penalties or even prison. DHS claimed more than 250,000 potential noncitizens were registered in four states but provided no names or methodology. Agents investigating individual cases repeatedly found false matches and people who had never registered or voted.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is turning DHS into an election enforcement operation built around his election lies. Federal agents are now pursuing voters and election officials months before the midterms, with states threatened with funding cuts and election officials threatened with prosecution if they resist.

entries.what_happened: A draft Trump proposal would exclude undocumented immigrants and broad categories of other noncitizens from the population count used to allocate seats in Congress and eliminate the collection of race and ethnicity data from the Census. The changes would likely shift representation away from Democratic-leaning states while eliminating data used to challenge racial discrimination in voting.

Trump’s Justice Department issued a legal opinion saying executive privilege can extend to private advisers who do not work for the federal government, potentially shielding their communications with Trump from congressional and legal investigations. The opinion comes months before the midterms, when a Democratic takeover of Congress will trigger investigations into Trump and his advisers.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s DOJ is expanding executive privilege to people who don’t even work for the government, creating another shield around his inner circle just as he faces the possibility of congressional investigations.

entries.what_happened: Trump is pursuing new ways to impose policies the Supreme Court recently blocked, including restrictions on birthright citizenship, efforts to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook, and new tariffs. After the Court upheld birthright citizenship, Trump said, “We’re ending it a different way.”
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is treating Supreme Court rulings as obstacles to get around rather than decisions he has to follow. If a president simply finds another way to do what the courts ruled he cannot do, judicial checks on presidential power become meaningless.

entries.what_happened: Trump’s DOJ deployed about 20 staffers to monitor voting in Hennepin and Ramsey counties during Minnesota’s primary, despite Hennepin County rejecting its request to place monitors inside polling locations. State law required the federal monitors to remain at least 100 feet from polling sites.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is pushing federal law enforcement deeper into state run elections months before the midterms. DOJ tried to put federal personnel inside polling places over the objections of local election officials.

entries.what_happened: The DOJ charged former Southern Poverty Law Center official Heidi Beirich with fraud, false statement, and money laundering conspiracies, expanding its criminal case against the civil rights organization. The indictment comes after whistleblowers alleged DOJ officials rushed the original case despite objections from career prosecutors.

State, local, and federal law enforcement fusion centers are monitoring social media accounts and planned events associated with opposition to Flock license plate surveillance cameras. Intelligence bulletins identified activists, listed cities participating in upcoming protests, and urged police to increase patrols around the cameras while linking the broader movement to separate acts of “vandalism.”
entries.why_it_matters: Government intelligence networks are tracking people organizing against mass surveillance and lumping lawful political activity together with criminal vandalism. Using government surveillance to track people protesting government surveillance is a great example of how a surveillance state operates.

entries.what_happened: ICE did not publicly report the death of Guatemalan immigrant Jose Chajon-Raxon, who suffered an apparent seizure one day after entering Delaney Hall and was released from ICE custody while hospitalized. Under a policy adopted this year, ICE no longer investigates or reports deaths occurring within 30 days after someone leaves its custody.
entries.why_it_matters: ICE can release critically ill detainees from custody and then avoid investigating or publicly reporting their deaths. The new policy creates a loophole that makes deaths connected to ICE detention easier to hide from Congress and the public.

entries.what_happened: ICE repeatedly force fed Kurdish asylum seeker and filmmaker Gabar Choli during a hunger strike, shackling and pinning him down while medical staff inserted a feeding tube through his nose and into his stomach. The practice continued intermittently for close to eight months, leaving him with injuries to his nose and esophagus, stomach problems, and psychological trauma.

Court filings show Kara Voorhies, an outside contractor described as FEMA’s “shadow administrator,” continued working inside DHS while being paid through a subcontracting chain involving a company owned by DOGE operative Kyle Schutt. Voorhies, who had no previous government experience, reviewed FEMA contracts and grants worth more than $100,000 while working alongside DOGE.
entries.why_it_matters: A DOGE operative had access to FEMA systems while his own company was being used to pay a contractor influencing FEMA spending. People with private financial interests were being given power over billions in government funds.

entries.what_happened: Doctors and medical organizations warn Trump’s overhaul of the childhood vaccine schedule will create confusion, increase vaccine hesitancy, and leave children vulnerable to preventable diseases. Trump called for separating and spacing out vaccines while again promoting conspiracies that childhood vaccines are linked to autism. This comes as the U.S. faces its largest measles outbreak in more than 30 years.

Trump made permanent a policy allowing the government to require visitors from 50 countries to post bonds of up to $20,000 for tourist or business visas. Visa issuances in those countries have fallen 83%, while overall overseas travel to the U.S. is down 4.3% this year and Canadian travel has fallen 25%.

Ukrainian drone operators defeated a U.S. armored brigade during a major Army exercise in Germany, locating vehicles and scoring simulated strikes so quickly that U.S. units had to be repeatedly returned to the exercise. The drill exposed U.S. vulnerabilities to the small drones that have transformed warfare in Ukraine.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump continues to attack Ukraine instead of taking advantage of the battlefield expertise it has offered to share. Now U.S. troops are facing the same drone attacks from Iran that Ukraine has spent years learning how to defeat.

entries.what_happened: Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is about 90% below prewar levels as Trump’s agreement with Iran to reopen the waterway remains stalled. Iran says it will not fully reopen the strait until the U.S. meets its demands, while an interim June agreement has collapsed.

Zelensky said Ukraine has only about 1% of the U.S. Patriot interceptor stockpile and is receiving 2.5 times fewer interceptors than in 2025, even as Russia has doubled its monthly ballistic missile attacks. He said 5% of U.S. stocks would protect Ukraine through the winter, while 10% would allow it to intercept all Russian ballistic missiles.

Workers’ inflation adjusted hourly earnings fell 0.1% in July as inflation wiped out wage gains. Annual inflation reached 3.4%, with fuel prices up 39.1% from a year ago as Trump’s Iran war and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz drives energy costs higher.

Trump’s Energy Information Administration raised its oil and gasoline price forecasts because of continued restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Gas is now projected to average $3.78 a gallon, up from $2.98 before the Iran war. Only eight vessels crossed the strait in a day compared with roughly 120 per day before the war.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump says the Strait of Hormuz is open, but his own government says restrictions are continuing and driving energy prices higher. Americans are paying the price for a war Trump claimed was over in March.

ICE has ramped up enforcement against Haitians in Ohio after Trump ended Temporary Protected Status for roughly 350,000 Haitians nationwide. In Springfield, Haitians who fled violence and built lives in the community are being summoned to ICE facilities and fitted with ankle monitors as they face possible deportation to Haiti.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump first targeted Springfield’s Haitian community with lies that fueled threats and neo-Nazi activity. Now his regime is stripping their legal protections and preparing to deport them to a country they fled because of extreme violence and instability.

entries.what_happened: The USS Abraham Lincoln has spent more than 250 days deployed and more than 200 consecutive days at sea during Trump’s Iran war, amid reports of supply shortages, plumbing problems, and deteriorating mental health. U.S. officials confirmed that a sailor went overboard August 3 in what the Navy considered a mental health episode and was rescued within an hour.
entries.why_it_matters: More than 5,000 sailors and Marines are paying the price for Trump’s Iran war, all while Hegseth fails to address deteriorating conditions and Trump mocks the troops complaining about them.

entries.what_happened: Senate Armed Services Committee ranking Democrat Richard Blumenthal demanded answers from Pentagon leaders after the USS Abraham Lincoln surpassed 250 days deployed and 200 days without a port call during Trump’s war with Iran.

The DOJ declined to block a federal court ruling allowing some Americans to possess silencers, short-barreled rifles, and short-barreled shotguns without registering them with the federal government. The ruling followed Trump’s 2025 tax law eliminating the $200 tax that had helped underpin federal regulation of the weapons since 1934.

DHS spent $464 million through a no-bid contract to buy 10 used aircraft it said were urgently needed for deportations, but most have barely been used. The contract went to a company whose chairman donated to a political committee supporting Kristi Noem, and three of the aircraft were luxury business jets.
entries.why_it_matters: DHS claimed an emergency to bypass competitive bidding, handed $464 million to a politically connected company, and then barely used the planes it supposedly urgently needed. This is another example of government waste and cronyism.

entries.what_happened: The VA has cut its backlog of disability claims from more than 400,000 in March 2024 to roughly 70,000, but veterans, attorneys, and VA employees say the push for faster decisions is producing basic and sometimes “egregious” errors. Pending higher-level reviews of denied claims have doubled since Trump took office.

Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz “under Iran’s control and management” after Trump claimed the U.S. has “total control” of the critical waterway and said, “I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT.” Most oil shipments through the strait remain blocked as the U.S. threatens further economic pressure against Tehran.
entries.why_it_matters: Months into Trump’s war, Iran still controls access to one of the world’s most important energy chokepoints while Trump claims the U.S. has “total control.” The standoff continues to disrupt oil supplies, drive up gas prices, and risk further regional escalation.

entries.what_happened: The U.S. military has lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones during Trump’s war with Iran, roughly 25% of its fleet and more than $1.3 billion worth of aircraft. The war has also depleted U.S. stocks of Tomahawk, Patriot, and THAAD missiles, forcing commanders to conserve some weapons.
entries.why_it_matters: Six months of Trump’s war have destroyed a quarter of America’s Reaper fleet and depleted critical missile stockpiles. The U.S. is burning through weapons and capabilities it may need for far more serious conflicts.

entries.what_happened: Putin made his first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, traveling to Iturup, one of four islands seized by the Soviet Union from Japan at the end of World War II. Japan summoned Russia’s ambassador, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the visit “absolutely unacceptable,” reaffirming Japan’s claim to the islands.

According to GasBuddy, the national average price of gasoline climbed above $4 a gallon. Prices have surged as Trump’s war with Iran and disruption of the Strait of Hormuz have constrained global oil supplies.

The federal budget deficit reached a record $432 billion in July, bringing the fiscal year deficit to $1.8 trillion with two months remaining. Customs receipts were negative for the third straight month as the government refunded tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court. The CBO projects tariff revenue will fall about $250 billion short of earlier estimates.

entries.what_happened: Trump cut CISA’s workforce by one-third and reduced its budget, while ending key intelligence-sharing and election-security programs. Now, amid his war with Iran, suspected Iran-linked hackers have targeted more than 30 U.S. water systems. At the same time, state election officials say they are receiving less federal intel as midterms approach.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump gutted the agency responsible for protecting U.S. infrastructure and elections, then went to war with a country capable of attacking both. Now American water systems are being targeted while election officials are being left without critical federal intel months before the midterms.

entries.what_happened: A Trump-appointed federal banking regulator conditionally approved a national bank charter for World Liberty Trust, part of the Trump family’s crypto business. The unprecedented decision allows the company, which is 38% owned by a Trump-affiliated entity, to directly issue its own dollar-backed stablecoin and profit from transactions while Trump remains president.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s government is granting regulatory approval to a business his family owns. He is yet again using the presidency to benefit his businesses via decisions made by the loyalists he installed in key agencies.

entries.what_happened: Trump deployed Homeland Security Investigations agents nationwide to search voter rolls for noncitizens despite internal warnings that the effort would produce large numbers of false matches and could violate federal privacy laws. From January 2025 through May 2026, fewer than 150 cases were referred for prosecution and only 41 people were charged with election-related crimes out of more than 150 million voters.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump sent federal agents to look for evidence to prove his election lies. They searched more than 150 million voters and found virtually nothing. His agencies did gain sweeping access to voter data as Trump tries to seize control over elections.

entries.what_happened: The Justice Department issued a legal opinion expanding the military’s authority to arrest migrants outside newly designated military zones along the southern border. The zones have already allowed troops to detain migrants for trespassing despite the Posse Comitatus Act’s longstanding restrictions on using the military for domestic law enforcement.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump continues to erase the line between the military and civilian law enforcement. His regime created military zones to give troops arrest powers and is now expanding where those powers can be used.

entries.what_happened: Federal prosecutors investigated Democratic fundraising firm Authentic Campaigns, formerly co-owned by the daughter of Judge Juan Merchan, who presided over Trump’s criminal trial. The investigation followed a referral from House Republicans who initially sought communications involving Kamala Harris, Joe Biden, Hakeem Jeffries, Adam Schiff, the DNC, and other prominent Democrats.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s DOJ used a criminal investigation to seek communications involving his political opponents and the family of the judge who oversaw his felony conviction. Trump promised retribution, and his Justice Department continues to deliver.

entries.what_happened: The Justice Department is shifting federal resources toward small-scale fraud cases. Meanwhile, Trump has pardoned or commuted the sentences of white-collar fraudsters, as the DOJ drops cases against corporations and wealthy executives.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s DOJ is prosecuting ordinary people for small fraud while Trump pardons wealthy fraudsters and his government drops cases against corporations and executives. This is another example of two systems of justice: one for the wealthy and powerful, and another one for everyone else.

entries.what_happened: FTC struck agreements with auto dealers accused of charging Black and Latino customers more. The FTC promised not to enforce parts of federal court orders requiring them to prevent credit discrimination and maintain fair-lending programs. They also made these deals without seeking court approval and, in at least one case, without notifying a state attorney general that had jointly brought the case.

The Pentagon is introducing a new Western civilization course for students in military-run schools that links Western history with Christianity. The curriculum uses materials from a conservative publisher and Hillsdale College and portrays Islam as more violent than Christianity. The Pentagon is also installing education officials tasked with expanding “patriotic values and classical learning.”
entries.why_it_matters: The Pentagon is bringing religion into government-run schools and deciding what version of American history children should be taught. And the “patriotic values and classical learning” sounds disturbingly familiar to Russia’s “patriotic education,” where the regime uses schools to indoctrinate children and teach them the version of history the state wants them to believe.

entries.what_happened: Immigration courts are scheduling large numbers of migrants for hearings on short notice, sometimes moving cases forward by months or even a year. Those who fail to appear can be ordered deported in absentia. Advocates warn that some people do not receive adequate notice and may not know they have removal orders.

Trump has dramatically expanded ICE’s 287(g) program, deputizing state and local police to interrogate and arrest people for immigration violations. Training for participating officers has been cut from about a month in person to just 40 hours online, while the program has faced lawsuits and complaints over racial profiling and wrongful detention.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is turning local police departments across the country into an extension of ICE while drastically cutting the training officers receive. A program already accused of racial profiling and wrongful detention is being rapidly expanded with no safeguards.

entries.what_happened: A federal judge refused to block Trump from moving forward with plans to build 62 miles of border wall across the Tohono O’odham Nation’s reservation in Arizona without the tribe’s consent. Tribal leaders say construction will destroy sacred sites, disrupt religious practices, and separate O’odham families and communities on opposite sides of the border.

The USS Abraham Lincoln has been at sea for almost nine months, including more than 200 days without a port call. There are reports of food shortages, plumbing problems, and deteriorating mental health conditions among sailors. Asked whether the deployment had gone on too long, Trump responded, “No, not nearly long enough.” Families of crew members condemned the conditions, as Democrats demand an investigation.

More than 5.3 million Americans have lost SNAP benefits since cuts went into effect from Trump’s 2025 tax and spending law. In Massachusetts alone, enrollment has fallen by roughly 182,000 people, including almost 65,000 children, as rising demand overwhelms the system.
entries.why_it_matters: More than 5 million Americans have lost food assistance because of Trump’s cuts. Families are losing help buying groceries so Trump can help pay for his massive tax cuts for the wealthy.

entries.what_happened: Trump’s response to the Iran war is drawing 172 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, pushing it below 300 million barrels for the first time since the early 1980s. Energy experts warn the rapid depletion could damage the underground storage caverns and weaken the reserve’s ability to respond quickly to another emergency.

The CDC has recorded 2,566 measles cases so far in 2026, the highest annual total in more than 35 years. Cases have been reported across 45 states and D.C. 93% of infections involved people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status was unknown.

U.S. and Arab intelligence indicates Iran used the two months after signing a June agreement with Trump to prepare for a broader war, accelerating missile and drone production, tightening Revolutionary Guard control over the military, and coordinating expanded attacks with militias in Iraq and Yemen. Iran also provided Gulf states with lists of energy facilities it threatened to destroy.

Trump ordered the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, citing Seoul’s refusal to join his war with Iran and calling the drills “hostile” toward North Korea. The decision came days after North Korea resumed ballistic missile tests while Trump praised his relationship with Kim Jong Un.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump is weakening America’s defenses and alliances around the world. He has strained relationships in Europe and the Middle East, drained military resources for his Iran war, and is now weakening U.S. defenses in Asia to punish another ally. At this point, it looks very strategic.

entries.what_happened: Texas-based Greenland Energy moved drilling equipment to Greenland’s eastern coast without Greenland’s authorization as it pursued plans to explore a potentially massive Arctic oil field. The move prompted a formal warning from Greenland, which has delayed the project until at least winter 2027.

U.S. allies including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain are frustrated with Trump’s handling of the Iran war and his failure to secure an end to the war. Some Gulf governments are questioning whether to continue hosting major U.S. military installations. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a new mutual defense agreement as they diversify their security partnerships.

The U.S. is pulling its last aircraft carrier from the western Pacific to support Trump’s war with Iran, leaving the region without a U.S. carrier as China increases military activity around Japan and the Philippines. The move comes as prolonged Middle East deployments are straining U.S. warships and crews.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s Iran war is draining U.S. military resources so badly that America is leaving the western Pacific without a carrier while China ramps up military activity around U.S. allies. Another gift to Xi.

entries.what_happened: Russia has built or expanded at least 10 drone bases near Ukraine and Belarus, installing 59 new launch rails for long-range attack drones. Some sites can launch newer Geran drones with ranges of roughly 620 miles, putting NATO territory within reach.

Back-to-school supplies are up 11% this year as Trump’s tariffs and rising energy costs from the Iran war push prices higher. Nearly half of parents expect to open a new credit card or increase their credit limit to cover school expenses.

entries.what_happened: Veterans and preservation groups are trying to stop Trump’s planned 250-foot triumphal arch at Memorial Circle between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. The National Capital Planning Commission has granted preliminary approval but has not yet given final approval.

The Justice Department plans to deploy roughly 1,000 monitors to polling locations for the November midterms, a record deployment. The move comes as Trump repeatedly claims Democrats will “cheat” and DOJ sues states for voter roll data.

Justice Department investigators sought interviews with law enforcement officials involved in the 2022 FBI search of Mar-a-Lago, expanding a Florida based inquiry seeking evidence of a “conspiracy” against Trump. The search recovered classified documents and led to criminal charges that were later dismissed.

The Pentagon quietly hired several conservative military influencers as civilian employees or special government workers while they continued publicly praising Hegseth and attacking his critics without disclosing their government roles. Some were assigned to Pentagon policy work, including a task force reviewing military education.

The Pentagon fired Stars and Stripes publisher Max Lederer, editor in chief Erik Slavin and reporter Lara Korte after Slavin and Korte publicly defended the editorial independence of the military outlet. The Pentagon had previously restricted the publication’s content and fired its ombudsman, whose job was to protect that independence.

Trump nominated four Republicans to the Postal Service’s governing board, breaking with the practice of bipartisan pairings, while pushing the agency to police mail voting. His executive order directs USPS to block mail ballots from states that do not comply with new voter verification requirements. The Supreme Court has allowed preparations for the restrictions to continue while the cases move through the courts.

A Postal Service whistleblower says USPS rushed to build a new system for Trump’s mail voting restrictions without full testing, warning that a single scanning error could cause entire batches of ballots to be rejected. The system was being prepared for the 2026 midterms despite ongoing court challenges.

Trump called on the Federal Communications Commission to investigate news organizations over polls he called “fake” and urged the agency to punish Meet the Press moderator Kristen Welker over reporting about his political endorsements. The FCC does not regulate polling and has limited authority over the content at issue.

The CDC said it had no records listing measles as the underlying cause of any U.S. deaths this year, disputing Pennsylvania’s attribution of two deaths to the disease. The statement came after CDC leadership reportedly directed officials to challenge the state’s reporting rather than follow the agency’s usual practice of accepting state data.
DHS Secretary Mullin said ICE could deploy to polling places if there is a “specific threat” or agents are serving a warrant on someone they have been tracking.

entries.what_happened: Election officials and judges are preparing for the possibility that federal agents could seek warrants to seize ballots or voting equipment during the midterms. One state has already held three statewide trainings, while election law experts issued guidance for judges on how to handle such requests.
entries.why_it_matters: We are weeks from the midterms and election officials are training for the unprecedented possibility of federal agents showing up and seizing ballots or voting machines. This will throw counting into chaos, break the chain of custody and threaten certification which is exactly what Trump wants to achieve.

entries.what_happened: Trump’s nine largest disclosed oil and gas holdings gained an estimated $1.5 million to $4.4 million between the eve of the Iran war and August 31. His accounts continued trading energy stocks during the war, including on days when his decisions moved oil markets.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump has millions invested in oil and gas while making decisions about a war that directly affects energy prices and the value of those investments. Even with outside managers controlling the trades, he is profiting from an industry directly affected by his decisions.

Trump said he would consider pardoning his former lawyer Michael Cohen, whose testimony helped prosecutors secure Trump’s 2024 felony conviction. Cohen is seeking a pardon and recently said he felt “pressured and coerced,” prompting Trump to praise him for “rectifying the situation.”

More than 20,000 ballots in Washington and 7,314 in Oregon were thrown out for late postmarks during this year’s primaries, even though many voters mailed them on time. Postal Service changes are delaying when some mail gets postmarked, with rural communities hit especially hard.

With the midterms just weeks away, election officials still don’t know what mail ballot rules they will need to follow. The Supreme Court is considering whether to allow Trump’s new restrictions to take effect, even as some states have already mailed ballots and the federal system needed to implement the rules is not yet ready.
entries.why_it_matters: This is part of Trump’s broader agenda to seize control over elections. Election officials from both parties warn the changes will disenfranchise voters, and Utah officials have called implementing them this late an “unmitigated disaster.”

entries.what_happened: Trump’s mail voting plan would require the Postal Service to screen ballots before delivering them to voters. States would have to submit voter lists to a new federal portal and use approved envelopes with barcodes that match those records. If they don’t, entire batches of ballots could be sent back instead of delivered. Two dozen states are challenging the plan.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump’s plan would allow the Postal Service to stop ballots from reaching Americans, giving the federal government a new role in deciding whose ballots get delivered.

entries.what_happened: Federal officers in Memphis arrested activist Hunter Demster while he was filming an immigration operation from 25 feet away. Demster says officers repeatedly pushed him farther from the scene until he refused to move again. He was then tackled and arrested under Tennessee’s Halo Law.

The Pentagon revoked longstanding protections for Stars and Stripes’ editorial independence, restricted what the military newspaper could publish, and purged editor-in-chief Erik Slavin, reporter Lara Korte and publisher Max Lederer after they publicly defended the paper’s independence. Slavin said he was fired after warning that refusing to publish an accurate story at the Pentagon’s direction would cross a “red line.”

ICE sent Adam Abdullah, a Somali asylum seeker who was living legally in Minnesota and has no criminal record, to Guantánamo Bay after arresting him during a traffic stop. Abdullah had a work permit and Social Security number and regularly checked in with ICE. He says authorities never explained why he was targeted. MPR independently confirms those core facts.
entries.why_it_matters: Abdullah was living legally in America, followed immigration rules and has no criminal record. Now he is being held at Guantánamo with limited access to his lawyer, without knowing why he was targeted.

entries.what_happened: An estimated 205,000 children have had a parent detained by immigration authorities since Trump returned to office, including roughly 145,000 U.S. citizen children. Some have been left with relatives or neighbors, missed school or medical care, and now live with the fear that a parent could be taken away.

ICE arrested Douglas Sura Cruz when he showed up for a routine green card interview with his U.S. citizen wife. Cruz had lived in the U.S. for 11 years, has two U.S. citizen children and no criminal record. A federal judge ruled that holding him without a bond hearing violated federal law and his constitutional due process rights, ordering the government to give him a hearing or release him.

entries.why_it_matters: The point of the intelligence community is to give a president an honest assessment of all threats. This reminds me of Russia, where Putin is surrounded by loyalists who afraid to tell him the truth.

entries.why_it_matters: The census determines congressional representation and federal funding. Excluding millions of residents would shift both, even though the Constitution requires House seats to be based on the “whole number of persons” in each state.

entries.why_it_matters: Iran is bringing its proxies together across the region, making it easier to strike U.S. allies, oil facilities and shipping routes from multiple countries at once.

The Pentagon has operational plans for a possible strike and has been examining capabilities against deeply buried targets. Trump has also repeatedly threatened to attack the site.

Starting Sept. 29, several Canadian products, including some alcohol, dairy products and motorcycles, will be banned from entering the U.S. He is also expanding 50% tariffs and ordering federal agencies to remove Canadian goods from government contracts.

Trump posted a map depicting Canada, Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, Greenland and Iceland under the American flag and labeled “United States of America.” Denmark condemned the image as “completely inappropriate,” while Iceland summoned the U.S. ambassador.
Trump said he had a “great conversation” with Putin and again insisted that Putin wants a deal to end the war. He blamed the lack of an agreement on Putin and Zelenskyy “hating” each other.
entries.why_it_matters: Trump continues to provide cover for Putin and Russia’s genocidal invasion. Russia invaded sovereign Ukraine, and Putin can end the war by withdrawing his forces. Framing the aggressor and the country defending itself as equally responsible normalizes Russia’s genocide and invasion.

entries.what_happened: After Putin and Trump’s phone call, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the U.S. should stop all support for Ukraine to help end Russia’s war. U.S. support has already dropped sharply since Trump returned to office, and now Moscow is openly demanding the U.S. cut off what is left.

Brent crude closed above $101 a barrel as fighting between the U.S. and Iran escalated in the Persian Gulf. U.S. gasoline hit a Labor Day record of $4.15 a gallon, while diesel is expected to reach $6 a gallon for the first time.

Treasury announced it would buy back $6 billion in longer term U.S. debt in an effort to calm the bond selloff and lower borrowing costs. The market barely budged with the 10-year Treasury yield climbing to nearly 4.86%, its highest in almost three years, while the 30-year remained above 5%.

entries.what_happened: The Supreme Court blocked Missouri from using its Republican-drawn congressional map in the November midterms. The unsigned order leaves the state to use its 2022 map for the midterms, which keeps intact a Kansas City-area seat that Democrats currently hold. The ruling also suspended a federal judge’s order that revived the GOP-favored map after Missouri’s Supreme Court ruled the new districts couldn’t take effect unless voters approved them in a referendum. Election officials, however, must now run the general election using different district lines than those used in the August primary.

A federal appeals court refused to let the Trump administration enforce new restrictions on mail-in ballots before the midterms, leaving in place an injunction blocking the U.S. Postal Service rule. The rule would require states to provide the Postal Service with voter information and unique ballot barcodes and would allow postal officials to return or refuse delivery of ballots that don’t comply. The three-judge panel concluded that the rule is likely unlawful because the Constitution gives states and Congress – not the executive branch – authority to regulate elections, and warned that implementing it now would “likely result in the disenfranchisement of millions of voters” while providing “minimal – if any – gains in combating voter fraud.”

Trump promised to send every American adult a $5,000 “Trump dividend” if Republicans retain control of Congress in the midterms. The proposal would cost more than $1 trillion, require congressional approval, exacerbate the nearly $1.8 trillion annual budget deficit, and lead to a rise in inflation. JD Vance, nevertheless, suggested that a “dividend for American workers” could be paid for by Trump’s tariff revenue. The cost of the dividend checks, however, would exceed the estimated $330 billion that the U.S. has collected from Trump’s tariffs.

The Trump administration plans to send $500 rebate checks to nearly 1 million Affordable Care Act enrollees in 30 states weeks before the November elections. The payments will go to people who bought coverage through HealthCare.gov without premium subsidies using surplus fees collected from insurers to operate the federal marketplace. The White House claimed without evidence that the Biden administration had “overcharged.” Health policy experts, however, said some of the surplus dates back to Trump’s first term. The administration didn’t explain how the $500 payment was calculated, and it’s unclear whether congressional approval is required.

Jimmy Kimmel moved his interview with Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico from ABC to YouTube after the FCC “threatened” ABC over “traditional editorial decisions.” Kimmel said the FCC “has threatened me, threatened our show, threatened our network, ABC, our affiliates, our local stations,” and explained that he pulled the broadcast “out of consideration” for affiliates that have to “deal with this nonsense.” Talarico is running in a competitive Texas Senate race against Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton. In January, the FCC changed its guidance on the equal-time rule, saying late-night and daytime talk shows are not automatically exempt from a requirement that broadcasters offer equal opportunities to political candidates running for the same office. And in April, the FCC ordered early license renewals for Disney’s eight ABC stations.

The prosecutor overseeing Trump’s “grand conspiracy” investigation resigned without bringing criminal charges. Joe diGenova’s investigation tried to establish that Obama- and Biden-era officials had engaged in a long-running criminal conspiracy against Trump to keep him out of office. Despite issuing dozens of subpoenas, no charges have been brought, and it’s unclear what evidence even supported the conspiracy theory. Justice Department had also officials reportedly lost confidence in diGenova’s leadership. When asked why he was leaving, diGenova replied: “I’m moving on.”

The Justice Department ordered election officials in 29 states and D.C., to preserve records from the 2024 election, warning that officials are under investigation and that failure to retain records could bring civil or criminal penalties. DOJ has also sued 30 states and D.C. seeking unredacted voter registration lists containing sensitive personal information.
entries.why_it_matters: DOJ is threatening state election officials with civil or criminal penalties while demanding sensitive voter data from an election held two years ago. This is part of Trump’s broader effort to sow distrust and take control over elections.

entries.what_happened: RFK Jr. is using military aircraft for domestic travel, including a trip to Iowa where he appeared with Republican candidates for the midterms. The Air Force aircraft used for the trip costs about $9,000 per flight hour, compared with approximately $250 for a commercial ticket between D.C. and Des Moines. The White House and HHS lawyers approved the arrangement.

Trump special envoy Steve Witkoff reported at least $257 million in income in 2025, including around $107 million from a holding company that included his stake in World Liberty Financial, the cryptocurrency business founded by the Trump and Witkoff families. An investment firm tied to the UAE bought nearly half of World Liberty while Witkoff was conducting Middle East diplomacy and meeting with the UAE national security adviser who backed the investment.
entries.why_it_matters: Witkoff went from Trump’s shady real estate friend to conducting U.S. foreign policy while making millions from private business interests tied to the countries he is negotiating with. This is yet another example of the mass corruption and cronyism in Trump’s regime.

Jim Pillen’s family business employed undocumented workers, including some who used fake or stolen identities. Latino civil rights groups, Common Cause and the city of Denver sued to block armed immigration agents from polling places, citing an 1865 federal law that prohibits federal officials from deploying “troops or armed men” where elections are being held. DHS says it is not planning operations targeting polling places but has said agents could appear to respond to “threats” or serve warrants.
entries.why_it_matters: This is part of Trump’s broader effort to seize control over elections. Putting armed federal agents anywhere near polling places is meant to cause fear and chaos.

entries.what_happened: Joe diGenova resigned five months after the DOJ brought him in to lead an investigation into former law enforcement and intelligence officials who investigated Russia and its attack on the 2016 election. His departure comes amid reported frustration inside DOJ and the White House over the pace of the probe, which has produced no charges.

Law enforcement agencies in Poland, Norway and Latvia say DOJ has not responded to requests for evidence in their Epstein investigations. Poland requested unredacted files in April as part of an investigation into possible ties between Epstein and Russian intelligence, while Norway and Latvia are pursuing separate criminal investigations.
entries.why_it_matters: European investigators are trying to uncover Epstein’s international network, including possible links to Russian intelligence, while DOJ continues to sit on evidence they requested months ago. Keeping those files from investigators keeps parts of Epstein’s network hidden.

entries.what_happened: Former immigration judge Chloe Dillon says she was fired two days after reporting that ICE had unlawfully detained an unaccompanied minor who had just appeared in her courtroom. In a whistleblower lawsuit, Dillon says a supervisor had also warned her that “the White House” was watching after she challenged an ICE policy she believed was illegal.

Around 3,000 children have been held at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas since family detention resumed in 2025, according to an attorney representing detained families. Some children have reportedly been held for months, with inadequate medical care, unsafe food and water, repeated illness and severe psychological distress. One 5-year-old reportedly tried to strangle himself after months in detention.
entries.why_it_matters: These are serious human rights abuses. Children are being held for months in conditions that are making them physically and psychologically sick. Immigration detention is not supposed to become indefinite punishment, especially for children.

entries.what_happened: Temporary Protected Status for about 200,000 Salvadorans who have been allowed to live and work legally in the U.S. since 2001 reached its expiration date Wednesday with DHS yet to announce whether the protections will continue.

The Army completed an investigation in July into the March 1 Iranian drone strike that killed six U.S. troops at a tactical operations center in Kuwait, but has not released its findings. The family of Army Reserve Capt. Cody Khork, one of those killed, is demanding the report and answers about potential security failures before the attack.

DOJ purged a federal prosecutor who worked on the fraud and bribery case against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani. The prosecutor had asked to withdraw after Trump officials moved to drop the charges. A federal judge later dismissed the case but called DOJ’s handling “highly unusual” and pointed to irregularities in how it was handled.

Trump officials are threatening medical schools with investigations, loss of federal funding and even their tax-exempt status over admissions policies meant to increase diversity. The regime says schools could be “breaking the law” even when they consider race-neutral factors like economic hardship if the goal is greater racial diversity. Courts have not settled that question.
